title: LatConnect 60 and Phi Earth Partner to Connect Space and Soil
summary: LatConnect 60 and Phi Earth have partnered to integrate satellite and ground-based environmental data for nature-based projects. The collaboration aims to bridge the gap between orbital observations and field measurements.

title: RTX’s Blue Canyon Technologies introduces new spacecraft mission enabler
summary: Blue Canyon Technologies, a subsidiary of RTX, has introduced a new spacecraft mission enabler. This development aims to enhance capabilities for small satellite missions.

title: The threat environment and processing at the edge
summary: SpaceNews interviews FrontGrade CTO Lorne Graves about how spacecraft processing power is adapting to megaconstellations and the benefits of satellite edge processing.

title: Propulsion is having a moment
summary: The article highlights the growing importance of propulsion in the space industry, featuring an interview with Kevin Lausten, CEO of Morpheus Space, at the 2026 Small Satellite Conference.

title: Space Angel secures $1.75m WA Government backing to advance Western Australian spaceport plans
summary: Space Angel received a $1.75 million grant from the Western Australian Government to advance plans for a spaceport. The funding was announced by Science and Innovation Minister Stephen Dawson.

title: Tendeg Launches NewTEN Steerable Compact Antenna at SmallSat
summary: Tendeg introduced NewTEN, a two-axis steerable compact antenna designed to enhance communications for small spacecraft. The product was unveiled at the SmallSat event in Salt Lake City.

title: Robotics and the future of on-orbit labor
summary: SpaceNews interviews Icarus Robotics CEO Ethan Barajas at the 2026 Small Satellite Conference about the role of robotics in future on-orbit labor. The discussion highlights advancements in space robotics for satellite servicing and maintenance.

title: Spirit Electronics Adds Texas Instruments and Microchip Technology Space Grade Components to Online Store Ahead of SmallSat 2026
summary: Spirit Electronics has added space-grade components from Texas Instruments and Microchip Technology to its online store in preparation for SmallSat 2026. This move aims to support performance-driven aerospace and defense programs with high-reliability electronics.

title: The Fuel for the Next Generation of Cislunar Exploration? Technology and Talent.
summary: The article discusses the future of cislunar exploration, highlighting the importance of technology and talent in advancing space missions beyond Earth's orbit. It reflects on the legacy of the Apollo moon landing and its impact on scientific and national security advancements.

title: Tory Bruno Named Honorary Chair Of World Space Week 2027
summary: Tory Bruno, President of National Security at Blue Origin, has been named Honorary Chair of World Space Week 2027. The announcement was made by the World Space Week Association.

title: From spy satellite to space telescope: The unlikely origins of NASA's Roman Space Telescope
summary: NASA's Roman Space Telescope is repurposing components from old spy satellites to create a next-generation space telescope. This unexpected reuse of hardware highlights a unique collaboration between national security and scientific exploration.

title: Astronomers discover hot watery exoplanet destined to be swallowed by its star
summary: Astronomers have discovered a water-rich exoplanet orbiting extremely close to its parent star, destined to collide and be consumed by the star. The planet's proximity to the star ensures a fatal end in the near future.

title: A black star in a false Spanish twilight: Here's the story of my 1st total solar eclipse
summary: The article describes a personal experience witnessing the August 12 total solar eclipse in Spain. It highlights the journey of a group of citizen scientists to observe the event.

title: Massive space mirrors could be 40 times brighter than the full moon, astronomers warn. 'It will be worse than big cities like London'
summary: A study warns that space mirrors proposed by U.S. startup Reflect Orbital could be 40 times brighter than the full moon, severely impacting the night sky. Astronomers say this would be worse than light pollution in major cities like London.

title: Chance gaze at old Hubble Telescope image leads to discovery that could reveal dark matter's secrets
summary: A former scientist discovered a significant clue about dark matter by re-examining an old Hubble Telescope image during a train commute. This unexpected finding could provide new insights into the mysterious substance.

title: On this day in space! Aug. 26, 1978: Sigmund Jähn becomes 1st German in space
summary: Sigmund Jähn became the first German to fly in space on Aug. 26, 1978. This historic mission marked a significant milestone for Germany in space exploration.

title: Heat shield under fire | Space photo of the day for Aug. 26, 2026
summary: A small satellite is facing destruction due to a failing heat shield. The issue was highlighted in a space photo from August 26, 2026.

title: 'Star Wars: Zero Company' review: XCOM-like strategically recaptures the magic of your favorite Star Wars films
summary: A review of 'Star Wars: Zero Company' highlights its XCOM-like strategic combat and a smaller-stakes Star Wars story that captures the essence of the franchise. The game is praised for blending familiar elements in a fresh way.

title: SpaceX's final Falcon 9 Starlink launch from Florida creates gorgeous 'jellyfish' over New York City (video)
summary: SpaceX's final Falcon 9 Starlink launch from Florida created a glowing 'jellyfish' effect visible over New York City. The launch marked the end of a series of Starlink missions from Florida.

title: SpaceX sends Starlink satellites to orbit on predawn launch from California
summary: SpaceX launched 27 Starlink broadband satellites into orbit from California's central coast in a predawn mission. This marks another deployment in the company's growing Starlink constellation.

title: Soyuz MS-28 departs the ISS, three spacewalks install upgrades to solar arrays and antennae
summary: Soyuz MS-28 departed the International Space Station after completing its mission. Three spacewalks were conducted to install upgrades to the station's solar arrays and antennae.

title: Starbase, Louisiana: The Largest Private Spaceport in the World
summary: SpaceX has announced plans to develop 'Starbase, Louisiana,' which will be the largest private spaceport in the world. This initiative marks a significant expansion of SpaceX's launch infrastructure beyond its existing facilities.

title: Starbase’s future production capacity ramping up
summary: Starbase's production site has seen increased activity to boost future production capacity. The developments are aimed at scaling up manufacturing capabilities at the facility.

title: Launch Preview: Falcon Heavy to launch Roman telescope, Falcon 9 to launch Starlink satellites
summary: Falcon Heavy is set to launch the Roman Space Telescope, while Falcon 9 will deploy Starlink satellites this week. Five orbital launches are planned from China, the United States, and French Guiana.

title: NASA’s Roman telescope nears launch, reaches final integration and rehearsal milestones
summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is nearing its launch, scheduled for August 30, after reaching final integration and rehearsal milestones.

title: LandSpace’s Zhuque-3 topples following milestone landing
summary: LandSpace's Zhuque-3 rocket toppled after achieving a significant milestone with a successful landing. This marks a major advancement for China's commercial spaceflight sector.

title: Ship 41 Completes Engine Testing Ahead of Flight 14
summary: Ship 41 has completed engine testing in preparation for Flight 14. Ship 40 is being transported back to Starbase from Christmas Island.

title: Stoke Space conducts second stage fit checks, completes first stage engines ahead of Nova debut
summary: Stoke Space has completed second stage fit checks and first stage engine assembly for its Nova rocket, aiming for a debut launch in 2026. This positions the company as a competitor in the fully reusable launch vehicle market.

title: Zhuque-3 Completes Second Flight with Successful First-Stage Landing
summary: LandSpace's Zhuque-3 rocket completed its second flight, achieving a successful first-stage landing. This milestone marks a significant advancement for the company's reusable rocket technology.

title: Ship 40 arrives at Christmas Island, Plans Return to Starbase
summary: SpaceX has successfully guided Starship Ship 40 to a location near Christmas Island. The company plans to return the ship to Starbase for further operations.

title: ESA Delivers: 50 years booklet
summary: ESA celebrates 50 years with a booklet highlighting 50 major achievements. The publication marks five decades of the European Space Agency's contributions to space exploration.

title: Phoenix 3: concept study for a reusable European spacecraft
summary: Engineers from ESA and industry partners completed a concept study for Phoenix 3, a reusable spacecraft for microgravity experiments and Earth return.

title: Proba-3’s eclipse hours before totality in Europe
summary: The Proba-3 mission will create an artificial solar eclipse to study the Sun's corona just hours before the total solar eclipse in Europe. This mission aims to provide unprecedented observations of the Sun's outer atmosphere.

title: A double eclipse for Proba-3
summary: Proba-3 is set to experience a double eclipse as the Moon crosses its field of view. This event highlights the satellite's precise formation-flying capabilities.

title: How ESA mimics and models the 2026 total solar eclipse
summary: ESA is preparing for the 2026 total solar eclipse by using artificial eclipse missions and computer simulations to study the Sun's corona, which is otherwise difficult to observe due to the rarity and brevity of natural eclipses.

title: Your chance to run software in deep space on ESA's asteroid mission
summary: The European Space Agency is inviting European researchers and companies to run their software aboard the Hera mission, which will travel millions of kilometers into deep space. This opportunity allows for testing innovative software in a real deep-space environment.

title: From drone flight to sounding rocket
summary: A student-developed radar retroreflector technology was tested for the first time using a drone at ESTEC, the European Space Agency’s technical centre in the Netherlands. The payload was carried by the drone during its flight.

title: Earth and Proba-3’s Coronagraph play hide and seek
summary: ESA's Proba-3 mission will demonstrate formation flying with two satellites to create an artificial solar eclipse using a coronagraph. The mission aims to study the Sun's corona by blocking out the bright solar disk.

title: Meet space startups at ESA’s Industry Space Days
summary: ESA's Industry Space Days event on 16–17 September at ESA-ESTEC in the Netherlands will bring together space startups and industry leaders to exchange ideas, showcase capabilities, and explore collaboration opportunities.

title: SpaceX Announces New Starbase, Louisiana Spaceport
summary: SpaceX announced a new high-cadence launch site in Louisiana for future Starship operations, with Gwynne Shotwell and Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry present. This marks an expansion of SpaceX's Starbase facilities beyond Texas.

title: Exclusive: City Labs Plans Second Nuclear Demo
summary: City Labs is planning a second nuclear demo after the success of its first nuclear-powered betavoltaic demo. The upcoming demo will feature a radioisotope heating unit.

title: White House Wants 1,000 Annual Launches and Reentries by 2030
summary: The White House has released a new National Space Transportation Policy aiming for 1,000 annual launches and reentries by 2030, replacing the 2013 policy. This initiative seeks to significantly boost U.S. space transportation capabilities.

title: The Aerospace Corp’s Disksat Gains Commercial Traction
summary: The Aerospace Corporation's DiskSat, a novel box-less satellite design, is gaining commercial interest. This innovative configuration is proving to be a successful departure from traditional satellite structures.

title: Exclusive: OrbitAID to Launch RPO Demo in 2027
summary: OrbitAID plans to launch a demonstration mission in 2027 to test the entire satellite life extension process, including both far-range inspection and close-approach maneuvering, in a single flight. This mission aims to qualify the full sequence of RPO (Rendezvous and Proximity Operations) for the first time.

title: Beyond Reach Labs Unveils Flarewing Deployable Solar Arrays
summary: Beyond Reach Labs has introduced Flarewing, a patent-pending deployable solar array system designed to fold flat during launch. This innovation aims to enhance solar power generation for space missions.

title: Starcloud Announces $250M Series A Extension
summary: Starcloud has raised an additional $250 million in a Series A extension, increasing its total valuation to $2.3 billion.

title: Letara Raises ¥2.6B to Build its Hybrid Rocket Engine Tech
summary: Japanese propulsion startup Letara raised ¥2.6 billion ($16 million) in a pre-Series A funding round to develop its low-cost hybrid rocket engine technology.

title: SpaceWERX Announces 2026 STRATFI Awardees
summary: Space Force announced the newest awardees of the SpaceWERX Strategic Funding Increase (STRATFI) program during the Fed Supernova conference. The awards were revealed as part of efforts to advance space technology and innovation.

title: Op-ed: The Technologies That Could Define the Future of Space
summary: Daniel Biedermann, a partner at NewSpace Capital, shares insights on key technologies shaping the future of space tech. The op-ed highlights emerging innovations that could define the next era of space exploration and industry.

title: LeoLabs to Provide Space Force With Surveillance Radar
summary: LeoLabs secured a $20.7 million contract with the U.S. Space Force to deliver a modified Scout containerized space surveillance radar. The contract aims to enhance space domain awareness capabilities.

title: TraCSS Traffic Coordination System Remains in Pilot Mode Due to Budget ‘Uncertainty’
summary: TraCSS, the space traffic management system by the Office of Space Commerce, remains in pilot mode due to budget uncertainty. The system has onboarded over 70 satellite operators and 10 nations.

title: NOAA Contracts Muon Space, Weather Stream, and Spire for TMATE Project
summary: NOAA awarded contracts to Muon Space, Weather Stream, and Spire Global to develop new weather satellite instruments for the TMATE project. This initiative aims to enhance weather data collection and forecasting capabilities.

title: Lyntris Targets Faster Delivery Timelines in Smallsat Interview With Madison Dye
summary: Lyntris, a new defense tech company formed by the merger of Vitesse Systems and Accelint, aims to improve delivery timelines for small satellites. The company focuses on supporting defense and national security missions in space.

title: Impulse Space Scales Rideshare Program to GEO With Increased Demand
summary: Impulse Space has fully booked three rideshare missions to Geostationary Orbit (GEO) through 2028 due to increased demand. The company is now considering doubling its rideshare missions to meet this growing interest.

title: Redwire to Manufacture Edge Aerospace Data Processing Units in US
summary: Edge Aerospace has partnered with Redwire to manufacture its data processing units (DPUs) in the U.S. under a licensing agreement. Redwire will handle the production of these units, expanding Edge Aerospace's manufacturing capabilities.

title: CesiumAstro Acquires 1Aardvark, Its 3rd Defense Systems Acquisition This Year
summary: CesiumAstro acquired 1Aardvark, a Virginia-based mission software and defense systems engineering company, marking its third defense systems acquisition this year. The acquisition aims to enhance CesiumAstro's satellite and communications capabilities.

title: TrustPoint Aces C-band GNSS Interference Demo for U.S. Naval Air Systems Command
summary: TrustPoint successfully demonstrated its C-band GNSS interference capabilities under a contract with the U.S. Naval Air Systems Command. This milestone highlights the company's advancements in space-based positioning and navigation solutions.

title: SSC Space Execs Talk Ground Service and Lunar Mission Growth at Smallsat
summary: SSC Space executives discussed ground services and lunar mission growth at the Small Satellite Conference. The interview highlighted the company's offerings in these areas.

title: NanoAvionics Upgrades its Flagship MP42 Bus Line, Adding a 500kg Platform
summary: Kongsberg NanoAvionics has upgraded its MP42 satellite bus line with a new 500 kg platform, making it the company's largest offering. The upgrade expands the capabilities of the MP42 line for larger payload missions.
